He was clearly asked whether he saw or heard anything relating to that matter, and as -- it was as a result of a fair objection of the Prosecution that he should be asked in that way. He was asked whether he had seen or heard. He was not asked whether he had any such belief. So I think that the Defence should be quoted correctly when put questions in re-examination and perhaps the transcript should be used to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that your point has been made by asking the previous question, so there's no need to digging into this matter any more. It is so obvious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked about your awareness of killings by other people, other soldiers, in Grabovica. How many people did you hear were killed in Grabovica on around the 8th and 9th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the Zadro family, Pero and Marica, and the two corpses that I saw lying on the ground. I don't know about anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is what you heard at the time about the deaths of other villagers. What did you hear about how many people had been killed? Apart from the ones you had seen yourself.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your question. These victims that I just mentioned are the only ones I know about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the recordkeeping system of the 1st Corps and the 9th Motorised Brigade in relation to the location of its soldiers at various times?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There again, Your Honour, I think it's the fourth time I have to stand up in relation to that matter. I'm sorry to do so so often, but this is the same line of questioning and it has nothing to do with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I -- I resist that objection very strongly. It does. It relates directly to the cross-examination. He was asked about the record. A record was produced. I'm not asking him about that. I'm asking about his knowledge of the recordkeeping system within the 1st Corps and whether he knew whether or not the soldiers who were in Grabovica could have been located. He may know; he may not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the first part of the question is relevant, but the second part in relation to the location of the soldiers at various times is not related. So you may just put the first question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour's ruling is that I can't ask him about whether he knew the recordkeeping extended to where soldiers were sent to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You could ask a question whether the witness is aware of the recordkeeping system of the 1st Corps, but you cannot ask the following questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sakrak, you heard the question. Were you aware or what was your awareness of the recordkeeping systems within the 1st Corps, and more specifically, the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything you know of from the system of military discipline and the command structure within the 9th Motorised Brigade that could have prevented the military police or military security service from finding you and interrogating you and other soldiers about what happened in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- I think the objection will be very obvious to Your Honour. I've raised it previously. And the question is just put in a different manner. The witness was not cross-examined about any investigation that would concern him. He was asked about his arrest. That's all that came out of cross-examination. This line of re-examination does not come out of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you may skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness has given evidence -- or was questioned about when he was arrested and when he was interrogated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that's the second time. Very late.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may ask some questions about he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already told us that you were arrested, I think, in 2003 and charged in relation to these particular murders. Was there anything that prevented you being arrested between --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it's exactly the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re did not finish his question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything to your knowledge that prevented you being arrested or investigated for the offences you committed between September 1993 and August 2003, when you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, now I can object and I can do so on three bases: It is not coming out of cross-examination; and it is speculative; and Mr. -- I didn't ask Mr. Sakrak about his arrest in 2003 but in relation to his having pleaded guilty. The question in essence, and the most important issue is in relation to the objections, that they do not come of cross-examination and, as I said, they are totally speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But this question is related to his arrest in 2000. We will allow this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sakrak, I repeat the question, and it's this: Was there anything to your knowledge that prevented you being arrested or investigated for the offences you committed in September 1993 between then and August 2003, when you were arrested and charged?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I can think of is that I was not actually a member of that unit and they couldn't reach me. They couldn't get to me. And naturally, I didn't turn myself in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you still in the same company when you returned from Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was a change.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Sead Karagic and Haris Reich -- Rajkic? Did they stay in the same -- did they go with you to the new company or remain in the old one?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, they transferred, but they were not in the same company as I. A new classification had been introduced and we were no longer in the same company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were ever investigated or interrogated in September 1993 for what they had done with you in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because -- I don't know, because we didn't keep in touch that much. We didn't keep in touch enough to discuss that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked about the criminal reputation or -- or the criminal -- the reputation alleged or otherwise of criminal behaviour of the 9th Brigade in Sarajevo. What was Celo's reputation at the time?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he was a good fighting man and not a criminal, as imputed by some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "imputed by some," do you mean imputed by some at the time?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in our parts. What I mean is the way they seemed to be treated here, the whole unit, including Rasim Delalic [as interpreted]. And from what I know, that unit was a good unit. It consisted of good fighting men, not criminals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a unit you were in?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the eight men that I served with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You answered in cross-examination that -- or it was put to you that there were between four and five thousand people in the 9th Motorised Brigade. How many of these people did you know -- personally know?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot. I knew many, many people. And many of these people had family ties through intermarriage, and I really don't see how anybody can claim that these people inspired fear or threatened members of each other's families. They are talked about here in a totally different way than they were known at the time in our locality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know how many units were in the 9th Motorised Brigade and the names of those units?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there again it's not something that comes out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. That's like re-presenting the evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The reason I was putting that goes to the witness's knowledge of the structure of the unit and, hence, what people in it were doing and, hence, how many people he knew or didn't know whether or not they were criminals, because it was a very general proposition put to him in cross-examination, and I just wished to make it slightly more specific to find out the extent of the witness's knowledge of how many people were in the brigades and whether in fact there were criminals and how many he knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You should have done that in your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of whether members of the 9th Brigade had criminal records? Was it something within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that anybody had a criminal past.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's nothing further. But I make it clear that I deliberately didn't lead that evidence. It wasn't part of our case with this witness. It was raised by the Defence in cross-examination. But that's the end of my redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Judge El Mahdi, please. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to ask you for clarification because I want to make sure that I have understood you correctly. My first question relates to what was raised by the Defence in relation with the Trebevic operation. You stated with regard to that operation, you stated that a number of members from the 9th Brigade were detained and you stated that as part of that operation, some of these people were questioned about the events in Grabovica. Would you be in a position to remember some of the names, the names of those members who were questioned about the events in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the names exactly now, but I know there was a number of people who were arrested at the time. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. But then how can you confirm that these people were questioned about, among other things, the events in Grabovica? How can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that because there were a couple of people from my company, such as Nihad Vlahovljak. He was questioned on that score. And a couple of other men were questioned to the same events. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Can you please make an effort and do you remember any other names apart from Nihad?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the unit in which I served, I can remember Nihad, Klos, Hajre, and I really can't remember any more names. Plus the men -- all of the men from the other base. I believe it was called the Romanija base. All of them together were taken into custody. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Can you give us a percentage of the members of your unit that were questioned about the events in Grabovica? Fifty? Sixty of you? Sorry, there were about 50, 60 of you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that around 70 per cent were questioned. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. But this did not lead to an indictment being drawn up in relation to the events.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it resulted in an indictment one way or another. I cannot confirm that. All I know is that people were questioned. But I would like to make one thing clear: I made sure to distance myself from all that, and I stayed away from these men on purpose. I didn't want to get involved, so I didn't get to know a lot about it. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I understand. My second question is in relation to the fact that Mr. Delalic showed an interest in finding those who had committed the murder of the parents of the two children. You stated that you did not take part in the identification of the suspected people, those who were suspected of having committed these murders. My question is the following: For you was it clear that your commander was serious, was determined and serious and really wanted to find out and arrest those who had committed these murders? What impression did you get? What impression did you get from the attitude of your commander? What sort of impact or effect did it have on you and, if you know, if you talked about other members of your company, what impact, what effect did it have on the other members of your company?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for me personally, as I said before, I spent most of the time inside the house, in my room, and I didn't wish to be found at that moment because I assumed that the perpetrator would be very fiercely punished. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, but that was not my question. What impact -- it was a message. It was a message. It was about how serious these events were, and also it showed that the commander was very serious, that he really wanted to find those who had committed these murders and in order to punish them possibly. Was it -- did you get that message from this?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to find the perpetrators. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, in order to punish them.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] What impact, if you're in a position to answer my question, but what sort of impact did this have on you, on the members of your unit? Did they get the same message? Did they understand that the commander did not in any way agree with that -- the sort of attitude that had been shown there?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they did. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] You believe so, but based on what? Did you talk about it with your fellow soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody was very happy about all that. Everybody was afraid for himself, because our superior was very angry because of everything that had happened. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] My last question: When you heard Nihad, who -- that amounted to allowing such acts, you were not, however, convinced that orders had been given in that sense.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: One might say that. I didn't know exactly whether the order had been issued or not. I can't be 100 per cent certain. But because I knew Nihad very well, I know he wouldn't have done something like that on his own. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, but that feeling, that impression, when you think back -- when you -- do you come to a different conclusion? Do you now think that everything came from him, or do you still maintain what you said at the beginning, that all this was due to orders given by somebody higher up?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say "someone higher up," I'm not talking about the top of the army. It could be someone who was just superior to him. I am not saying that the order arrived from the forward command post. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And who, for example? When you had that impression, that feeling, who did you think about at that time, at that specific time? Who did you think about?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't thinking of anyone in particular at the time. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, witness. [In English] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge El Mahdi. Any questions out of Judge's question?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: A very short one, Your Honour, if I may. Further cross-examination by Mr. Mettraux:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sakrak, you've been asked by His Honour about the effect which Celo's line-up might have had on other soldiers, other than you. And you stated, if I'm correct, that you assumed that it would have had the same effect on others. Is it correct that, apart from you, sir, Haris Rajkic and Sead Karagic were also hiding in the house together with you on that day when you had committed the crimes?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that all of you were hiding from Celo?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. There is something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think needs to be clarified, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When Judge El Mahdi asked his question -- my second question, I'm quoting is in relation to the fact that Mr. Delalic showed an interest in finding those who had committed the murder of the parents of the two children. Down two lines: "My question is the following: For you was it clear that your commander was serious -- was determined and serious and really wanted to find out and arrest those who committed these murders?" I think the witness's evidence has been that the commander was Nihad. If I could just clarify that with the witness, whether he understood by that question that Celo was the commander or whether it was someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I can clarify that very easily by withdrawing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the best person to clarify this issue is Judge El Mahdi himself. Questioned by the Court: 22 JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] No, I was not referring to Nihad. I was thinking of the commander, of the one who was in charge and who took the initiative and who called the men, who called the troops to detain and to arrest those who were suspected of having committed this murder. And I believe that the witness understood me perfectly well and I believe that my question was very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My question was in the same sense, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm not -- I have no issue with Your Honour's question. Your Honour's question was entirely clear. It's just that it says several times "your commander," and the witness's evidence so far has been that Nihad was the commander. And Your Honour referred to Celo. Perhaps if the witness could clarify whether he understood Your Honour's question to mean -- be referring to Celo as his commander or someone else. That's my only concern, that we might have -- at the end of the case, there might be different submissions as to who the witness thought was the commander -- his commander. JUDGE EL MAHDI: In my opinion, the witness understood me very well. But I think if you want to clarify more this question, I think you -- you can put a question, only one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Further examination by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sakrak, when His Honour Judge El Mahdi talked about Celo as your commander, were you understanding -- or who did you understand to be "your commander" by His Honour's question?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramiz Delalic, in the context of this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At this stage, are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We are not clear whether the documents -- we believe the document 965, which would be the log, has already been admitted. We just want confirmation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it has.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. And a set of picture which we marked for identification. We tendered those, I think, and my colleague --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: They've been admitted as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No document from the Prosecution side, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. When we are adjourned and -- the guard will show you out of the room. We wish you a very pleasant journey back home. The hearing for today is adjourned and we'll -- Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, when you asked me about documents, it was only the photographs, unless they haven't been tendered. If they're tendered ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe so. I believe all the documents has been admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So I have to remind the parties next week we will sit in the morning session for the whole week. The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
